title: Neural histology reveals NASH treatment-response signals missed by ordinal staging
summary: Neural biopsy analysis quantified heterogeneous fibrosis in NASH trials. A threshold derived from STELLAR data identified fibrosis responses in 27% of 63 cilofexor-plus-firsocostat recipients versus 5% of 37 placebo recipients in ATLAS, where manual staging did not show a significant difference. This retrospective secondary analysis does not reverse the original trial endpoint or establish clinical treatment benefit; findings depend on the selected response threshold.
ai_technology: Deep convolutional neural network; DELTA Liver Fibrosis score

source_review.scope: Primary relevant Methods/results/limitations, exact primary front identity and current primary PubMed notice metadata; version dates distinguished.

evidence.tested: Patient-separated histology development/testing, an ATLAS-only test cohort and retrospective treatment-response/clinical-progression analyses.
evidence.unknown: Prospective endpoint validation and clinical outcome benefit remain unestablished; significance depends on the response threshold and post-hoc analysis.
evidence.ai_role: Residual/inception-inspired CNNs quantify pixel-level fibrosis patterns; a distribution-change score measures treatment-associated tissue changes.
